sites.meaning: Set the per-core USB mode byte to host mode (1). Stock is 3 (device). The driver loads it at RVA 0x44C0 (`adrp x8,0x14000 ; add x8,x8,#0x3f4 ; ldrb w8,[x8,x9]`) and dispatches through the jump table at RVA 0x10360: mode 1 lands at 0x4500 and stores 8 into *(void**)(usbc+0x18); the guard at 0x477C (`subs w8,w8,#0x8 ; b.ne`) only falls through to the host start path - UsbCoreIfc->StartController at 0x47AC, or the local UsbStartController at 0x4A70 - when that value is 8, while stock mode 3 stores 0x20 and never takes it.
sites.evidence: Our mode array is `03 00 00 00` immediately before the ASCII "usbc" struct base at 0x143F8 (stride 0x130), the same placement as bitra/9707f (`03 03` before "usbc" at 0x15360). bitra UsbConfigDxe.hostmode.efi and 9707f UsbConfigDxe.patched.efi change exactly those bytes 03 -> 01, and our whole mode-switch block 0x4480-0x4680 is byte-identical to giulia's stock build.

sites.meaning: Pass mode argument 1 instead of 0 to the USB core start entry (`mov w1,wzr ; blr x8` becomes `mov w1,#1 ; blr x8`) on the host start path the mode byte selects.
sites.evidence: Same edit exists in bitra UsbConfigDxe.hostmode.efi (both copies of the call, at 0x4638 and 0x472C); our build has this one copy at 0x47A8. The driver's own fallback start path at 0x47D8 already passes w1 = 1 to the local UsbStartController, so 1 is the value this code treats as "start".

limitations: Mode 1 provably selects the in-driver host start path; it does not by itself prove that the SM8650 DWC3 controller enumerates as a host. The driver still decides the role at runtime from the UsbCoreIfc protocol state, and VBUS control goes through the PMIC, which this build leaves inert, so a bus-powered device may still not appear. The IOMMU attach gate at RVA 0x561C is deliberately left stock: in our build the flag byte 0x148B9 is zero in the file, so that branch is already taken and the giulia edit would only skip a failure log.
